title: Emergence of Boolean Facts from Markovian Coarse-Graining in Relational Quantum Causal Processes
abstract: We formulate an operator-algebraic mechanism by which exact Boolean records can arise from local completely positive quantum operations without being imposed as microscopic structure. The kinematic input is an algebraic process functional assigning probabilities to local normal completely positive operations in a finite operational context. From the predual response of a target algebra to source interventions, relative to a background strategy class, we define an influence algebra; exact events are then, by definition, the projections in its center. The dynamical question is whether nontrivial centers can be generated by coarse-graining rather than inserted through split-record laboratories. We address this question using state-preserving normal unital completely positive coarse-graining channels. If the Cesaro means of such a channel converge to a Choi-Effros infrared range and the range is asymptotically abelian in the GNS seminorm, then the represented infrared algebra is a commutative von Neumann algebra. Its projection lattice is therefore a complete Boolean algebra. We also give a finite-sector block-primitive criterion, motivated by locality and scrambling, which implies this asymptotic abelianness with exponential suppression of off-sector coherences and intra-sector fluctuations. The result is a conservative mathematical statement: classical facts are not identified with arbitrary projections of a Type-III local algebra, but with central projections selected by an asymptotically abelian completely positive infrared limit.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates the emergence of classical Boolean facts from complex quantum dynamics using algebraic methods. It shows that if a system undergoes repeated, state-preserving coarse-graining, the resulting macroscopic structure will possess classical (Boolean) properties only if the limiting algebra is asymptotically abelian. This provides a mathematical constraint on how 'classicality' can arise naturally in fundamental quantum theories.
main_problem: The central question is whether classical Boolean facts can emerge naturally from local, completely positive quantum operations (coarse-graining) without being imposed as fundamental axioms.
main_result: If the coarse-graining process leads to an infrared range that is asymptotically abelian, then the resulting algebra of 'exact' macroscopic events forms a complete Boolean algebra.
method: The analysis uses operator algebras, defining an 'influence algebra' based on quantum causal processes and examining the limit (Cesaro mean) of repeated coarse-graining channels.
model_or_system: The framework is built upon Relational Quantum Causal Processes (RQCP), involving local von Neumann algebras subjected to state-preserving normal unital completely positive coarse-graining channels ($\Gamma$).
key_observables: Exact events are identified as projections within the center of the influence algebra, $	ext{Proj}(\mathcal{Z}(I_{C;B}^Y))$, and the key diagnostic is the asymptotic abelianness of the infrared range.
important_parameters: The convergence rate ($\gamma$) in exponential suppression estimates, and the limit $N 	o \infty$ for the Cesaro averages.
main_assumptions: The result relies on assuming state-preserving normal unital completely positive coarse-graining channels and requires the infrared range to be asymptotically abelian.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the algebraic machinery for identifying events via influence algebras. It then analyzes the dynamics using Markovian coarse-graining, culminating in theorems that link asymptotic abelianness of the resulting algebra to the structure being a complete Boolean algebra.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical criterion—asymptotic commutativity under coarse-graining—for when quantum correlations naturally collapse into classical probabilistic structures, which is highly relevant for understanding decoherence and measurement in open quantum systems.
